tasks.title: Build interactive reserved-seat map for Tagos Puso
tasks.next_action: Run preflight against the latest EVNTS staging branch and confirm all five Railway staging app services are green before starting Stage 1.
tasks.source: ChatGPT task generated for ChatGPT Agents Tab Manager
tasks.goal: Upgrade the existing EVNTS reserved-seating system into a complete visual seat-selection experience for Tagos Puso. Buyers who have completed Stripe payment should open a secure interactive venue map, automatically focus on seats eligible for their purchased ticket tier, select exactly the number of seats covered by their paid entitlements, obtain concurrency-safe temporary holds, see a live assigned-versus-purchased counter and hold countdown, then confirm seats and receive final QR tickets.
audit_focus: Existing SeatSection, SeatRow, Seat, SeatTierEligibility, SeatHold, SeatAssignment and SeatSelectionAccess models
Existing seat map, hold and assignment APIs
Current Ticketing Settings and Ticketing Operations UI
Existing ticket-tier configuration and Stripe payment flow
Existing ticket issuance, QR, email and scanner infrastructure
Responsive mobile and desktop seat-selection behavior
reference_facts: The reserved-seating backend already exists and must be reused rather than rebuilt.
Paid seat selection already uses secure expiring SeatSelectionAccess tokens.
Temporary SeatHold records, expiry handling, concurrency protection and final SeatAssignment records already exist.
The current frontend renders seats as section and row grids inside static/js/ticketing.js.
The current admin UI can view, block and unblock existing seats but cannot create sections, rows, seats, map coordinates or tier eligibility.
Seat already supports map_x and map_y.
SeatTierEligibility already controls which ticket tiers can use a seat.
The Tagos seat diagram identifies Silver $150, Gold $200, VIP $250 and VVIP $500 areas.

The reconstructed diagram appears to contain 771 visible seat boxes while previously sourced venue capacity was 760. Do not import the reconstructed production seat inventory until that discrepancy is verified.
Do not fabricate exact Scottish Rite seating geometry.
Generic synthetic seat fixtures are allowed for automated tests but must be clearly test-only.
required_deliverables: Seat Inventory configuration UI under event ticketing
JSON seat-map importer with validation and preview before commit
Section, row, seat, blocked-state and tier-eligibility management
Normalized seat-map geometry using existing map_x and map_y fields
Event-level seat-map canvas configuration including stage orientation
Enriched public seat-map API with coordinates, eligibility, assignment counts and tier requirements
Interactive SVG-based seating canvas
Automatic fit-to-view and focus on the purchased ticket tier
Zoom in, zoom out, pan and reset or fit controls
Touch-friendly mobile pan and zoom behavior
Visible Available, Selected, Held, Sold, Blocked and Not Eligible seat states
Persistent live counter showing seats assigned over tickets purchased
Per-tier assignment counters for mixed-tier orders
Immediate server-backed seat holds when eligible seats are selected
Concurrency-safe handling when another buyer acquires a seat first
Live hold countdown based on server hold expiry
Seat-state refresh without full-page reload
Confirmation disabled until every paid active entitlement has an eligible seat
Compact selected-seat summary before confirmation
Final assignment using existing SeatAssignment logic
Existing QR ticket issuance and delivery after seat confirmation
Regression coverage for importer validation, eligibility, holds, concurrency, counters, assignment, expiry and idempotency
Final staging end-to-end acceptance test
All five Railway staging app services green after every staging merge
instructions: Work as one long-running autonomous agent task. Complete one stage at a time and use continuation messages instead of spawning parallel implementation agents.
Repository: melencio-ai/evnts.
Railway project: caring-dream.
Target environment: staging only.
Target Git branch for completed work: staging.
Production is NOT authorized.
Never merge to main.
Never modify or redeploy the production environment.
Before every implementation stage, branch from the latest staging branch.
Keep every stage focused and reviewable.
Reuse existing EVNTS seat, ticketing, payment, QR, scanner, email, Celery, export, authentication and event-scoped permission infrastructure.
Do not rewrite the existing reserved-seating backend.
Use additive, backward-compatible schema changes only when required.
Do not reset or replace existing databases.
Do not copy production data into staging.
Do not import the reconstructed 771-seat Tagos seat map into staging as authoritative venue inventory until the seat-count discrepancy is verified.
The seat importer may use generic test fixtures for validation.
Prefer SVG for the interactive venue canvas because seats need individual interaction, labels, accessibility and responsive scaling.
Do not introduce a heavy frontend framework unless the current vanilla JavaScript architecture cannot safely support the required interaction.
The host marketing website remains separate. EVNTS owns ticketing, payments, seat selection, assignment, QR issuance and scanner validation.
Seat eligibility must be enforced by the backend. Frontend disabled states are not a security boundary.
A buyer may never select or assign more seats than valid paid active entitlements.
For mixed-tier orders, each entitlement may only be assigned a seat allowed for that entitlement's tier.
Seats outside the buyer's eligible tiers should remain visible for venue context but must be disabled and visually marked Not Eligible.
Temporary holds must remain concurrency-safe and server authoritative.
Do not release permanently assigned seats when temporary holds expire.
The client-side countdown is informational only. Server expiry remains authoritative.
Do not require a full page reload to reflect seat-state changes.
Use item-level or map-state refreshes instead.
Run relevant automated tests and Django checks before every pull request.
Add regression tests for every changed behavior.
MERGE/DEPLOY GATE: after every merge into staging, immediately stop all feature coding.
Identify the merged commit SHA and monitor Railway project caring-dream, environment staging.
Check staging app services: web, worker, beat, quotation and quotation-v2.
Do not recreate or modify Postgres or Redis just to satisfy the deployment gate.
Do not begin the next implementation stage until all five staging app services report SUCCESS.
If any service reports INITIALIZING, QUEUED, BUILDING or DEPLOYING, do not perform new feature work.
When a deployment is still in progress, end the response with exactly: AGENT_STATUS: CONTINUE and NEXT_ACTION: Recheck the Railway staging deployment; do not start new feature work yet.
If a staging deployment reports FAILED or CRASHED, inspect logs, diagnose the smallest safe fix, branch from latest staging, test, merge the fix into staging, then restart the same Railway gate.
A merge is not considered complete until its Railway staging deployment is green.
Only use AGENT_STATUS: BLOCKED for a genuine external blocker such as missing permissions, credentials or verified venue data that prevents the next safe implementation step.
Missing final Scottish Rite geometry must not block implementation of the reusable seat-map platform, importer, canvas or test fixtures.
Only use AGENT_STATUS: COMPLETE after every stage, final staging E2E acceptance and final Railway staging deployment succeed.
At the very end of every response, include exactly these two machine-readable lines:
AGENT_STATUS: CONTINUE | COMPLETE | BLOCKED
NEXT_ACTION: <short next action or blocker>

subtasks.title: Add live assignment counters, immediate holds and countdown
instructions: Branch from latest staging only after Stage 3 Railway gate is green.
Add a persistent counter such as '2 of 4 tickets assigned'.
For mixed-tier orders show per-tier counters and a total counter.
Selecting an eligible available seat should immediately request a server-backed temporary hold instead of waiting for a separate bulk Hold button.
If a competing buyer acquires the seat first, update that seat to Held or Sold and show a clear conflict message.
Deselecting should release the buyer's temporary hold safely when appropriate.
Display remaining hold time using server-provided hold_expires_at.
The countdown must never override server expiry.
Refresh seat states approximately every 5 seconds or with an equivalent lightweight item-level refresh.
Do not reload the full page.
Refreshes must not erase the buyer's valid selections.
Keep existing transactional locking and uniqueness constraints.
Add tests for immediate hold creation, competing buyers, release, expiry and counter updates.
Run checks and tests.
Open PR, merge to staging, then enforce Railway deployment gate.

Add tests for incomplete confirmation, exact completion, mixed tiers, repeated confirmation and ticket issuance exactly once.
Run checks and tests.

Verify secure seat-access token handling.
